name: LizCraft
line: A signature with a softer edge.
intro: An identity built around a sculpted monogram, an expressive serif wordmark, and a blue-and-gold palette. The result is a visual language that carries from the smallest mark to the shopping bag.
focus: Logo design, visual identity, brand pattern, packaging application
details: A recognisable signature
The letter L sits inside a softly irregular frame. Repeated contours extend that frame into a graphic language of its own.
Consistency, with room to move
Horizontal and vertical signatures, a standalone monogram, and a recurring contour pattern give the identity a flexible set of expressions.

name: Beans Central
intro: A bright, approachable identity for a food brand. A playful bean-and-fork symbol, rounded typography, and a confident red create a consistent frame for a menu full of personality.
focus: Logo design, colour system, typography, social campaign assets
details: Small symbol, big appetite
The illustrated bean becomes the anchor of a friendly signature. Red, warm yellow, and deep brown build a palette that feels closely connected to the food.
A system made for a menu
Bold curved headlines and generous food photography give each dish a moment of its own, while keeping the campaign recognisably connected.

name: Natoral
intro: A compact identity with a leaf-like symbol and a rounded wordmark. Deep green, fresh lime, and pale mint establish a visual connection to nature without overcomplicating the mark.
focus: Logo design, colour variations, repeat pattern
details: An identity that grows
The layered symbol brings together a simple natural silhouette and a distinctive rhythm of rounded forms.
From mark to pattern
Repeating the symbol creates a vivid brand texture. A set of colour variations keeps the signature usable across light and dark applications.

name: Pure Hive Honey
line: A little warmth. A clear identity.
intro: An identity and packaging exploration for Pure Hive Honey. A geometric honey-inspired mark, warm amber tones, and a characterful wordmark bring the product and its visual identity together.
focus: Logo design, visual identity, packaging application
details: Rooted in the product
The mark references a honeycomb form and a flowing honey detail. The palette draws directly from the natural warmth of the product.
Made tangible
The identity is shown in a jar application, connecting the logo, label, and product photography as one composition.

name: Feasts & Flavours
intro: A food identity that pairs a bold ornamental symbol with lively lettering. Rich red and generous food imagery give the system an immediate, celebratory presence.
focus: Logo design, typography, colour system, branded food communication
details: A distinctive centrepiece
A symmetrical symbol creates a recognisable focal point, while the expressive wordmark keeps the overall identity warm and informal.
Colour that carries
Red acts as the common thread across varied food compositions, from quieter white layouts to full-colour campaign pieces.

name: Objects in perspective
intro: Independent modelling and rendering studies exploring familiar product forms. These pieces focus on shape, material, lighting, and composition, extending visual design into three dimensions.
details: Learning through making
A beverage can and personal-care bottles become studies in surface, proportion, reflection, and light.
Study, not commission
These are independent practice pieces using existing product identities. They do not imply a commission, affiliation, or endorsement from the featured brands.

name: Genesis Orb
line: A simple mark. A consistent system.
intro: A brand identity centred on a green-and-earth signature. The supplied identity guide defines logo arrangements, colour values, background usage, and clear examples of how the mark should be protected.
focus: Logo design, signature arrangements, brand usage guide
details: Structure and restraint
A circular green gesture and an angular earth-toned accent create the symbol. The wordmark brings a lighter typographic contrast.
A guide for consistency
The design extends into documented colour and logo-usage rules, helping the identity retain its proportions and character across applications.

name: Doc’s Apothecary
intro: A collection of product labels for hair and skin care. The work brings together product names, ingredients, directions, and brand elements within the constraints of small print formats.
focus: Packaging typography, product labels, print layout
details: Clarity at a small scale
Product information needs a clear hierarchy. Each label balances the brand signature with the practical information a customer needs.
A family of applications
The supplied label artwork spans different products and container formats. The collection is presented here as graphic and packaging design.

name: On paper
intro: Selected print work across company profiles, packaging, personal stationery, and music artwork. Each format asks for a different balance of image, typography, information, and pace.
focus: Editorial layout, print design, packaging, music artwork
details: Design beyond a screen
Print invites a more physical kind of attention: the scale of a title, the rhythm of a spread, the relationship between a cover and its contents.
Different formats, considered choices
This selection brings together a corporate profile, cocoa packaging, wedding stationery, and music artwork from the supplied portfolio.

name: In the feed
intro: Selected social and campaign visuals from the supplied portfolio. The work brings brand consistency, clear hierarchy, product imagery, and platform-specific composition into a fast-moving format.
focus: Social design, campaign assets, digital communication
details: Designed for the moment
A social visual needs to communicate quickly while still feeling like part of a recognisable brand.
Context matters
This collection includes brand work completed directly and through agency relationships. It is presented as a selection of visual executions, without invented performance results.

name: A birthday in motion
line: A small celebration, brought to life.
intro: A short personal birthday animation. A compact motion piece with a simple purpose: turn a greeting into a moment that feels special.
details: Play the piece
A short-format exploration of timing, transitions, and expressive movement.
